fm.hook: A consumer goods CEO in Mumbai tells your consulting engagement team: 'Our teams use ChatGPT all day to draft emails and slides, yet our operating margins have not moved by a single basis point. objectives: **Explain** why individual AI fluency fails to generate enterprise earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) without workflow redesign.
**Contrast** rule-based, predictive, and generative AI models across data requirements, cost structures, and error profiles.
**Apply** the core principles of token mechanics, contextual retrieval (RAG), and agentic workflows to business problem solving.
**Execute** the four-step audit protocol (prompt, review, challenge, decide) to prevent automation bias and catastrophic hallucinations.

title: Why models are confidently wrong

fm.title: Why models are confidently wrong

fm.hook: On the same set of fact questions, one AI model gets 24% right and another gets 22%. The first is also wrong 75% of the time; the second is wrong 26% of the time. A leaderboard that counts only right answers ranks the first one higher. Which would you let near a client deck, and why does the leaderboard disagree with you?
objectives: **Describe** the three stages that turn a text predictor into a chat assistant: pretraining, fine-tuning and feedback from human raters.
**Explain** why a model trained and graded this way produces confident, fluent falsehoods, and why newer models still do.
**Evaluate** an accuracy figure for an AI tool by asking what it counts as an error and what it does with "I don't know".
**Identify** where bias and invented facts can enter an AI use case, and who must check the output before it reaches a client.
